title: Recovery doctor console
description: Objective: implement project health, doctor checks, reconciliation inventory, backup/RPO, and exact recovery command surfaces. Deliverable: recovery/doctor modules. NOT in scope: optimistic auto-repair or browser-executed disaster restore. Hard dependencies: Generated control-room client and Crash reconciliation services. Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/recovery/** and apps/control-room/src/doctor/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test.
definitionOfDone: HEALTHY, DEGRADED, and UNKNOWN_TRUTH are distinct and every check exposes stable ID/evidence/affected records.
Only daemon-supplied recovery commands are actionable; uncertainty disables mutation.
Backup cursor/RPO and orphan inventory limitations are explicit.
taskRails: The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength.
Every fact is text/icon/color encoded, keyboard accessible, provenance-drillable, and honest under degraded data.
IDE adapters remain thin optional launch/discover/embed shells with no product logic. Keep modules below 400 lines; explicit owned paths only.

implementationPlan.description: GREEN the doctor surface in doctor-console.tsx. Define closed presentation props—not daemon response DTOs—for the supplied overall health fact, ordered checks, view freshness/loading/degraded state, optional offline report timestamp/lock-proof facts, and non-authoritative suggested operations. Render cr.health.status, cr.health.check.{checkId}, and cr.health.doctor using Panel/FactRow so every claim retains its exact supplied truth/provenance and missing fields stay UNKNOWN. Preserve HEALTHY, DEGRADED, and UNKNOWN_TRUTH as distinct health outcomes without ranking or aggregating checks; never calculate SQLite compatibility or startup eligibility. Implement deterministic row focus for j/k and Enter callbacks without mutating order. Render the exact offline copy only for the supplied OFFLINE_READ_ONLY report, keep suggestions plain text, and expose no command, transport, parser, OS lock, filesystem, or repair behavior. Leave doctor-j1.tsx untouched and make the doctor suite green.
implementationPlan.note: doctor-console.tsx GREEN: `npx vitest run src/doctor/doctor-console.test.tsx` -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 25 passed (25), exit 0. 249 physical lines (wc -l), under the 250 target. Closed presentation props only (DoctorCheckPresentation, DoctorOfflineReport, DoctorConsoleProps) — no daemon response DTO, no parse, no transport. DOCTOR_HEALTH_OUTCOMES is the closed three-token set and statedOutcome() collapses anything else to a distinct OUTCOME_UNSUPPLIED="UNKNOWN" rather than to UNKNOWN_TRUTH, so "the daemon said nothing usable" never impersonates "the daemon reached an unknown-truth verdict". The overall outcome and each check's outcome are rendered from their own supplied token through the same HealthOutcome component (text + glyph + data-health, three channels); nothing reads `checks` to compute the overall, so a HEALTHY overall survives a failing check and a DEGRADED overall survives all-HEALTHY checks — both directions are pinned. Every claim routes through FactRow, so blank/whitespace values fail to UNKNOWN with the UNK chip and one chip travels with every fact. Fact IDs are check-qualified (health.check.{checkId}.{area|severity|evidence|affected.{index}}) so provenance IDs are unique across the surface. An empty affected list renders a null-fact UNKNOWN row rather than "none" — a check that named no record may equally have failed to enumerate, and only the daemon can distinguish those. Keyboard j/k/Enter clamps at both ends and never reorders `checks`. The §8.7 offline banner is assembled from two literal halves around the supplied time and renders ONLY when report.mode === "OFFLINE_READ_ONLY"; suggested operations render as LI text. No SQLite comparison, no startup-eligibility verdict, no command, no OS-lock or filesystem behavior anywhere in the module. doctor-j1.tsx is byte-untouched (absent from git status; shell/j1-flow.test.tsx still imports it unchanged).

Read useGating() directly, join each presentation to exactly one current NextAllowedCommand by commandId and exact target, and pass that original command plus the original presentation to onRequestConfirmation—never clone it, build an envelope, classify commands as safe, dedupe, or infer a control from health/lifecycle text. implementationPlan.note: recovery-actions.tsx GREEN: `npx vitest run src/recovery/recovery-actions.test.tsx` -> Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 22 passed (22), exit 0. 248 physical lines (wc -l), under the 250 target. RecoveryActionPresentation is a two-arm union discriminated by the optional `commandId`: RecoveryCommandPresentation names a commandId + exact targetAggregateId + supplied label/qualifier, RecoveryUnavailablePresentation carries a fully supplied RecoveryUnavailableReason (phrase, reasonCode, layer) plus the kind needed for a stable test ID. A presentation that matches nothing and explains nothing renders nothing (§8.1 absence over invented copy). resolve() filters useGating().commands on commandId AND targetAggregateId and returns a command only when exactly one matched — two matches is ambiguity, not a menu, and yields null. onRequestConfirmation receives the original frozen NextAllowedCommand and the original presentation object by reference (tests assert with toBe); nothing clones, wraps, envelopes, dedupes, classifies as safe, or infers a control from health or lifecycle text. enabled = actionsEnabled && authorityMode === "LIVE": actionsEnabled is used verbatim and OFFLINE_READ_ONLY/HISTORICAL/UNKNOWN each additionally fail closed, while useGating().stale is deliberately never read — a comment in the module says why (§8.6: a lagging view still shows commands the daemon returned and those revalidate on the daemon), and two tests pin that LAGGING and requiresAffordanceRefresh leave a live command enabled. Test ID grammar is cr.action.<dashed-kind>[.<qualifier>] from the RESOLVED command's kind (not the caller's claim), buttons are native and keyboard-reachable, and disabled controls stay visible per §6.3. Supplied disabled copy renders when the group is blocked and falls to UNKNOWN when unsupplied. Feedback renders only for currently-resolved command IDs, so a withdrawn command's stale outcome cannot linger; PENDING/CONFIRMED use role=status, the >2s line is the §12 verbatim constant, REFUSED uses role=alert and exposes the code and refusing layer, both falling to UNKNOWN when absent rather than minting a RuntimeError. The group carries data-recovery-actions so sibling surfaces can prove no control renders outside it.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review + 20 mutation drills, all from an OS temp location, all hash-restored, zero repo evidence.

ADVERSARIAL FINDINGS FIXED (three, none of which any mutant could have surfaced — they are missing cases, not wrong ones):
1. Blank identity join. resolve() compared presentation.commandId to command.commandId with no identity guard, so a payload that failed to name a command and a command whose ID failed to parse would have JOINED each other ("" === ""), granting a control from two absences. Fixed with identified() guards on both commandId and targetAggregateId; new test "never joins two unnamed identities, even if both sides are blank" builds a blank-ID command object bypassing the parser and asserts zero controls. This is `mem:gotcha-blank-string-renders-as-a-confident-empty-cell` applied to identity rather than display.
2. Nameless control. A blank supplied label rendered an empty button with an empty accessible name. The command arm now falls back to the daemon's own commandKind (the only other name in evidence, same choice frame.tsx makes) and the unavailable arm falls to UNKNOWN; new test pins textContent and aria-label become "recovery.complete".
3. Blank record in the canonical sentence. reconciliation narrative opened with a raw recordId, so a blank record produced " failed integrity checks during import: ...". Now uses node-authority's readIdentity(); new test pins "UNKNOWN failed integrity checks during import: ...".
Also hardened React keys: duplicate presentations or duplicate feedback entries previously collided on key (commandId); keys are now index-qualified. A new test pins that two identical presentations render TWO controls — the module must never deduplicate what the daemon returned.

CHECKLIST SWEEP: no production module sorts, reverses, splices or otherwise mutates an input array (grep-verified; the only .push calls are into module-local arrays). Empty arrays are covered in every position (checks, affected, presentations, feedback, rows, items, blindSpots, inventory) and each renders an explicit UNKNOWN or an explicit not-a-proof line rather than a confident empty. Keyboard clamps at both edges and returns early on an empty list, so no index can go out of range. No hand-written cr.chip.* anywhere (all chips come from the kernel via FactRow) and no cr.chip.policy-approved, so the fact==chip equality audits count only truth chips (`mem:gotcha-pol-chip-is-not-a-truth-chip`). No IO, timers, subscriptions or side effects on any path, so there is no error-path cleanup to miss. Duplicate daemon-supplied IDs produce duplicate DOM test IDs; that is deliberate — deduplicating would hide a daemon defect — and every test scopes its queries with within().

MUTATION DRILLS — 20 mutants, one at a time, each restored and sha256-verified identical before the next; final run KILLED=19 PROBLEM=0 plus one separate new-file drill: (1) coerce UNKNOWN_TRUTH to HEALTHY; (2) drop a check's evidence row; (3) render only the first affected ID; (4) turn an offline suggestion into a button; (5) drop target matching; (6) accept an ambiguous match; (7) ignore actionsEnabled; (8) ignore the non-live authority-mode guard; (9) blanket-block on useGating().stale; (10) blank the refusal layer while keeping the code; (11) hard-code a third reconciliation repair button; (12) render an empty orphan list as "No orphans remain"; (13) compute SQLite compatibility client-side; (14) compute outbox lag from the two cursors; (15) delete the post-cursor RPO sentence; (16) default backup byte verification to "complete"; (17) plant a `fetch(` token in a production module; (18) rename an exported anchor; (19) import ../fixtures.js; (20) add a new file to src/recovery. Each turned exactly one NAMED focused test red, and the harness independently failed any mutant whose anchor did not match or that left the file hash unchanged, so no drill could pass vacuously.

DEFECT FOUND BY DRILL 18 AND FIXED: the scan's anchors were bare prefixes ("export function RecoveryExternalInventory"), which still match a renamed "RecoveryExternalInventoryRenamed" — the mutant SURVIVED. Anchors now carry their opening parenthesis and the rename is killed. That is the plan's "verify the structural scan truly reads all four canonical production files from process.cwd()" catching a real hole rather than confirming a hope; drill 20 separately proves the exact-file-set assertion reddens when any new file appears in an owned directory.
